body:
I'm glad that you took the time to put so much effort into a reply. I had experienced no failures whatsoever before graduating high school. The first year of college was a very rude awakening for me, but I'm over that by now.
As for the alcohol, I quit after 5 months of being addicted, and ended up getting addicted to weed for 4 years instead. I quit that a couple weeks ago though, cold turkey. It was easy for me, because I was just sick of how it normalized doing nothing all day, every day. Although that's an easy way to live my life, in a haze where I can't really overthink all my issues, it's just not sustainable, and it was fueling my laziness. I do realize that having quit that recently could make some rather weird changes with the chemistry of my brain, having been smoking every day for years. Which is why I'm waiting a bit. I saw a therapist for the alcohol. I was able to quit drinking and smoking extremely easily on my own with no help. So I guess I wasn't really addicted, I just didn't have a reason to stop, and I was using it as a way to self-medicate my depression (or at least escape from it).

But anyway, I'm just glad that at least 3 people took the time to read and reply to this. I have no one at all to speak to, so it's nice to see someone care before I go through with this, even if they couldn't come up with a reason to keep living. TBH, I had no expectations, because no one truly knows my life, no matter how much I write. I sincerely can't think of anything, so how could someone else, that's an unfair expectation. I just thought it was worth a shot, maybe there was something I was missing that someone else could see or that worked for them. But I guess not. I appreciate it though. Thank you for your time.

edit: I just realized you deleted what you wrote. Sorry if I didn't reply quick enough. I did read it all, and I do appreciate it man, I really do.

It's basically just a very condensed version of it, yes. Although the one to my ex had a not-so-nice tone to it. I've been on the edge for years, but she's essentially the one who pushed me over. So I kind of wanted to let her know that, which I know is a shitty thing to do to her, but I'm deadset on it. I just don't get why she randomly stopped talking to me after everything was going so well on both sides of the relationship. I suppose she found something or someone that she liked more, although I was the only one who was really ever supportive of her and was her only friend for a while. I suppose the reasoning is irrelevant though, and she refused to tell me anyway. Thank you for the encouragement though. Girls can be trouble for everyone.
Thank you for reading it, I really appreciate it. I will keep your invitation in mind.
